The Collapse in South African Cricket

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Whats's wrong with South African cricket on & off the pitch, and how can it be fixed?

Unique Selling Point:
Along with the Springboks & Bafana Bafana, the Proteas are a national treasure, so when they do badly, the country shares its pain. The last year has been an annus horribilus for cricket in South Africa with the team struggling on the pitch and huge issues in the boardroom too. We look at the trials and tribulations of South African cricket and what can be done to fix it. We speak with interim CEO of Cricket South Africa Jacques Faul & Director of Cricket Graeme Smith

Summary:
The Proteas are at perhaps their lowest ebb since their return from international isolation in 1992. The Test Team is in the process of getting thrashed by England. This follows defeat by India and Sri Lanka in their last two series, a disastrous performance at the 2019 Cricket World Cup. Their Captain can’t buy a run, their best bowler Kagiso Rabada has been banned from the next test at the Wanderers this week for yet another disciplinary indiscretion.

Then there are issues with transformation - a continual problem for SA Cricket, with not enough black players in the team and a catastrophic brain drain of white players like Kyle Abbot, Rillee Rosseau, Duanne Olivier quitting the National Team for a Kolpak contract in the UK. Black interim Team direction Enoch Nkwe has effectively demoted for now Proteas coach Mark Boucher

And we cannot ignore the turmoil at Cricket South Africa. A projection R1 Billion loss, sponsors deserting cricket, the suspending of former CEO Thabang Moroe, animosity between administrators and the Player’s Union and the media…

What can be done to fix Cricket in South Africa and return the Proteas to past glories?



Expert:
Dr. Jacques Faul Interim CEO Cricket South Africa
Mr. Graeme Smith Director of Cricket
Mr. Enoch Nkwe Proteas Assistant Coach
Mrs. Firdose Moonda Cricket Journalist
Mr. Andrew Breetzke

Press Release:


The Wilting Proteas
The Proteas are a national treasure, but with a number of disastrous defeats on the pitch; major internal disputes in the boardroom and serious allegations of mismanagement and bad governance, Cricket South Africa is in a tailspin. Could the appointment of a new interim CEO and Director of Cricket finally put an end to the team’s decline? Carte Blanche sits down with the new appointees, who are now squarely in the firing line.
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


SCRIPT
V/O: Summer in South Africa is synonymous with cricket and this country’s love affair with the game is long & enduring.

The Proteas are a beacon of national pride. Over the years we’ve seen them scale the very heights of the game on the backs of heroes past.

But after years of success, a crisis the likes of which has never been seen before is befalling cricket.

Since 2019 The Proteas have suffered 3 consecutive test series losses, endured their worst ever World Cup and are struggling to replace a golden generation.

Off the field, CSA is drowning in debt, there are accusations of maladministration & sponsors are leaving

Now can new leaders like Jacques Faul & Graeme Smith rescue the game?

LINK: I’m here at the famous Wanderers bullring. This has been the scene for many a win for the Proteas over the years. But with the team struggling on the field and turmoil in the boardroom, how long will it take before they’re able to taste victory once more?


V/O: Over the past year, there’s been a precipitous decline in the fortunes of the Proteas, witnessed by journalist Firdose Moonda

· The poor performance of the team in 2019

· Retirements & Kolpak

V/O: Chastened by a disastrous World Cup, CSA fired coach Otis Gibson and appointed Enoch Nkwe as interim head coach for one of the most daunting assignments in world cricket: a tour of India.

· Enoch leading the team a 0-3 defeat



V/O: The Proteas were whitewashed by a rampant Indian team and returned to South Africa to much uncertainty because of problems in the boardroom.

· Firdose outlines some of the rows and ructions that have plagued the administration of the game over the past 2 years

V/O: The major issue off the field is a financial one. CSA’s inability to secure a broadcast deal led to the failure of the proposed Global T20 league overseen by former CEO Haroon Lorgat.

This has been compounded by 2 seasons of the loss-making Mzansi Super League, draining the financial resources of a once cash-flush administration.

· Firdose Comment













V/O: Faced with the prospect of huge financial losses, the board led by CEO Thabang Moroe looked for ways to save money.

The members council of CSA unilaterally decided to restructure domestic cricket, increasing the number of first class teams from 6 to 12. This brought them into conflict with the South African Cricketers Association. Their CEO Andrew Breetzke takes up the story.

· Andrew Breetzke on how the relationship with Cricket SA devolved resulting in SACA taking legal action

V/O: At war with SACA and facing mounting scrutiny from the media, things came to a head in December when Moroe revoked the accreditation of several journalists igniting a firestorm.

· Firdose & Andrew on having accreditation revoked and the resulting cascade: Sponsors resign, CEO suspended







V/O: Carte Blanche requested an interview with Thabang Moroe but he said that he has been asked by CSA to refrain from making any comments to the media.

V/O: That was when Jacques Faul was appointed interim CEO, a position he held previously in 2012.


V/O: That was when Jacques Faul was appointed interim CEO of CSA, a position he held previously in 2012.


· We talk about the 4 metrics of success: Proteas, Sponsorship, Players, Pipeline – they are all in trouble

V/O: With the England Series just weeks away, his top priority was to appoint a director of cricket. He turned to South Africa’s most successful captain, Graeme Smith


· His vision for the team

· His appointment of Mark Boucher as coach


V/O: Interim Head Coach Enoch Nkwe was asked to take on the role of Assistant Coach

· Enoch on being shattered on the demotion but deciding to take the role anyway





V/O: The Proteas began the English series with victory in the first test but 3 subsequent defeats have shown just how much work is needed to get the team winning consistently again

V/O: It is off the field that Jacques Faul faces the biggest challenge. Over the next 4 years CSA is projecting a loss of R750 million.

· Comment about projected losses

V/O: He has also begun to repair the relationship with SACA

Jacques & Andrew on repairing relationships

V/O: It’s been reported that the members council may rescind the decision to restructure domestic cricket. This has been welcomed by SACA

But is this enough to appease sponsors like Standard Bank whose decision not to renew their sponsorship will cost CSA R73 million per year?

· On the impact of Standard Bank leaving cricket and what it will take to bring sponsors back to the game

V/O: With cricket in crisis, can it be turned around?

· Jacques admitting that mistakes have been made and needing to be honest and more open with all stakeholders in cricket


CLOSING: These are indeed worrying times and it will not be fixed overnight. But with a youthful team drawing on the experience of coach Mark Boucher and Director of Cricket Graeme Smith, hope springs eternal.

Constructive engagement between CSA & SACA has been welcomed

After all no one wants cricket to fail in South Africa and summer just wouldn’t be the same without it.
